new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Only one work was listed and it was the quoted one, so no silent/not-opened works existed to spot-check. As a substitute I extracted the whole 1903-page atlas text (extracted text, ionice -c3) and searched for 'pidgin French', 'French pidgin', 'pidgin fran', 'French-based pidgin'. Hits: p. 481-482 (ch. 035 references: Hollyman 1964a; Hollyman 1971 'Tay Boi: notes on the pidgin French of Vietnam'; Stageberg 1956 'Pidgin French grammar: a sketch' -- both Vietnam), p. 696 = book p. 475 ('Pidgin French and Pidgin English in New Caledonia' as plantation languages, ch. on English-derived contact languages), p. 698 = book p. 477 (Bislama replaced on the New Caledonian mainland 'by pidgin French, a…

sources.citation: Hollyman, K. J. 1976. "Les pidgins européens de la région calédonienne". Te Reo 19: 25–65.
sources.note: Socio-historical and lexical study with 34 attested pidgin sentences and contemporary comments; no phonology/prosody section. The only 'accentuation' remark (p. 38) concerns French final-syllable stress on the loanword canaque (< Hawaiian kanaka) as an etymological argument, not the pidgin's stress. Silent on word stress.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page and reference record 318664 (hh:ld:Hollyman:Nouvelle-Caledonie) for newc1245
sources.note: Glottolog lists exactly one reference (Hollyman 1964, doctype 'minimal'/a wordlist or less, 8 pp.); language marked extinct, no coordinates. Its Wikidata link Q3083202 resolves to 'New Caledonian French' (fr-NC regional French), a mismatch with the pidgin.

sources.citation: Wurm, S. A., P. Mühlhäusler & D. T. Tryon (eds.). 1996. Atlas of Languages of Intercultural Communication in the Pacific, Asia, and the Americas. Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter. DOI 10.1515/9783110819724 (chapter: Ehrhart-Kneher & Corne, 'The Creole language Tayo and language contact in the Far South region of New Caledonia', pp. 265–270, DOI 10.1515/9783110819724.2.265)
sources.note: CrossRef record only; De Gruyter page not fetchable (405/202 empty). Unknown whether it says anything about the pidgin's phonology.

sources.citation: Chaudenson, Robert. 1994. Review of Ehrhart, Le créole français de Saint-Louis (le tayo) en Nouvelle-Calédonie. Études Créoles 17(1): 128–142.
sources.note: Review of the Tayo grammar; no mention of the earlier pidgin or of stress (direct download summary of the Persée page).

sources.citation: Corne, Chris. 1989. "Un créole à base lexicale française en Nouvelle-Calédonie : le tayo ou le patois de Saint-Louis". Études Créoles 12(2): 29–42.
sources.note: Different language (Tayo, tayo1238). Phonology notes (§2.0) on Tayo consonants/vowels only; no stress statement. Cites Hollyman 1964/1976 and rejects the idea that Tayo is a relexification of the local pidgin ('Les dates et surtout la configuration socio-linguistique ne s'y prêtent pas'). Bibliography gives Hollyman 1971 'French in the Pacific', CTL 8: 903–27.

sources.citation: Hollyman, K. J. 1964. "L'ancien pidgin français parlé en Nouvelle-Calédonie". Journal de la Société des Océanistes 20: 57–64. DOI 10.3406/jso.1964.1901
sources.note: Phonology section (p. 59) covers only vowels (timbre and length unknown), consonants (prenasalised b/d, s~tj, p for v) and CV syllable shape; nothing on stress or accent. Only prosodic remark: interrogatives 'caractérisée seulement par l'intonation' (p. 63, §5.6). Glottolog's sole descriptive reference (Glottolog's most extensive description, 'a wordlist or less').

sources.citation: O'Reilly, Patrick. 1953. "Le français parlé en Nouvelle-Calédonie. Apports étrangers et vocables nouveaux. Archaïsmes et expressions familières". Journal de la Société des Océanistes 9: 203–228.
sources.note: About Caledonian regional French vocabulary; notes pidgin-English (bichelamar) loanwords (caï-caï, picaniny, poca…) and that pidgin English 'n'est plus, pratiquement, parlé'; the word 'accent' occurs only as 'prononcé avec l'accent du cru' (p. 221). Nothing on stress.
